newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine judge rejects Cavallo's apology.
newsitem.headline: Argentine judge rejects Cavallo's apology.

text.p: An Argentine Supreme Court judge who was called corrupt by ex-Economy Minister Domingo Cavallo on Tuesday rejected his apologies and said he will insist that the former outspoken official be tried in court.

"It's too late now," judge Augusto Belluscio told reporters after Cavallo retracted from his accusations made in 1993, when he was still in the cabinet, that the judge was "corrupt" and had probably stolen court files.
Federal judge Adolfo Bagnasco, in charge of the Cavallo-Belluscio case, will have to rule whether Cavallo's apology suffices or whether to start trial procedures.
The trial for alleged slander and offense was due to open Thursday, but Belluscio said Bagnasco will now need more time to study the merits of Cavallo's apology.

"I have no interest whatsoever in the retraction," Belluscio said. "What I am interested in is that sanctions contemplated by the penal code for an offense of the magnitude committed by that gentleman be applied," the Supreme Court judge said.

Cavallo, who last July was sacked by President Carlos Menem after one too many brawls over his tough austerity plan, in October 1993 said a lost file in a case involving the Central Bank was "probably stolen" by Belluscio and a second judge. He also called both "corrupt".
The other magistrate accepted an earlier Cavallo apology. But Belluscio Tuesday rejected a second excuse presented by the former minister in an attempt to head off the trial.
